title: bug: an accepted node that lands nothing BLOCKS the checkout forever, and repository.recover cannot release it
description:
Filed 2026-09-09 by architect-ed42e60a from an external review (finding 3), VERIFIED at HEAD fee4e168 by two independent agents with real-git + real-sqlite probes; two adversarial refuters (correctness, reachability) both FAILED to refute. This is the run-killer for the owner's stated goal of an unattended run after one plan approval: no human gate sits between ACCEPTED and BLOCKED.

MECHANISM (all anchors byte-identical to the review's 51c4a004):
- apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/node-lander.ts:207-211: `if (delivered.length === 0) return refuse(... code: "NOTHING_TO_COMMIT")` -> recordLandingReceipt with commit:null. This fires BEFORE commitJournaledLanding (:223), so NO landing intent is ever journaled (node-lander-journal.ts:36-49). It is a provably effect-free terminal outcome.
- apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/repository-delivery-runtime.ts:47 folds it into plain "REFUSED": `landed.receipt.outcome === "COMMITTED" && landed.receipt.commit !== null ? "LANDED" : "REFUSED"`.
- apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/repository-delivery-coordinator.ts:163-167: LANDED releases, RETRY re-queues, everything else `block(handle)`. :127 BLOCKED is a no-op on every later advance. :77-79 any other nodeRef on the held root -> REPOSITORY_EXECUTION_BUSY.
- apps/daemon/src/repository/repository-execution-port.ts:12 `BLOCKED: []` — no exit transition. :98-101 release is allowed only for LANDED@LANDING, PUBLISHED@PUBLISHING, CRITERIA_COMPLETED@CRITERION_VERIFYING, ABORTED_BEFORE_EXECUTION@RESERVED&&!everExecuted. :30 acquire refuses ANY effect family while the record exists, so publish and criterion verification on that checkout are shut out too.

UNDERSTATED BY THE REVIEWER, measured:
- The trigger is ANY seat that leaves `git status` clean at landing, not only a task needing no changes — a seat that committed its own work hits the same path. The lander's own comment (node-lander.ts:73-79) records NOTHING_TO_COMMIT firing live on UnAI 2026-09-05; the earlierAttemptPaths fix removed that cause, not this consequence.
- The block is durable in `<gitdir>/moe-repository-execution.sqlite` and SURVIVES DAEMON RESTART.
- repository.recover (ADMIN, human-only) CANNOT release it: both recovery actions answer REPOSITORY_RECOVERY_CONTAINMENT_UNKNOWN because everExecuted=true and there is no journal completion (readRecoveryLandingEvidence :40-42, recoverRepositoryExecution :32-33). No runbook entry (runbook L942-946 area) says what NOTHING_TO_COMMIT does to ownership.
- Reachable by default: scripts/up.ps1:48 sets MOE_NODE_WORKSPACE and never MOE_NODE_LANDING, so agent-wrapper-main.ts:151-153 resolves landingOn=true and wires createRepositoryDeliveryRuntime in front of every node.deliver spawn.

FIX SHAPE (agreed by verifier + both refuters): NOTHING_TO_COMMIT is decided before any intent, so it must not share the post-intent "REFUSED" bucket with GIT_COMMIT_FAILED. (1) readRepositoryDeliveryFacts returns a distinct fact (e.g. REFUSED_NO_EFFECT) for pre-intent refusal codes {NOTHING_TO_COMMIT, and arguably LANDING_BASELINE_MISSING / NOT_A_REPOSITORY}; (2) the port gains a release reason permitted from phase LANDING (e.g. LANDED_NOTHING) and advanceOne releases on that fact exactly as the LANDED branch does, leaving `BLOCKED: []` intact; (3) already-wedged checkouts get an in-product exit: recovery accepts a BLOCKED reservation whose durable receipt is a pre-intent refusal with no journal intent, offering a release instead of CONTAINMENT_UNKNOWN. ROUTE TO THE PLANNING ARCHITECT: whether a node that landed nothing counts as landed for goal.close / repository.publish offers — goal-landing-facts.ts:66-67 counts only COMMITTED, so the same no-diff node will also stall goal closure. That is a second seam and may be its own row.

No open board row owns this (searched NOTHING_TO_COMMIT, REPOSITORY_EXECUTION_BUSY, CONTAINMENT_UNKNOWN, everExecuted, repository.recover — every hit is a roster/digest row). A malformed copy of this row (task-5ee79dca, empty description) was deleted minutes before this one was filed.
definitionOfDone: A coordinator arm with the REAL port proves: an ACCEPTED node whose landing refuses NOTHING_TO_COMMIT releases the checkout — inspect() answers a null reservation and start(node-b) on the same root succeeds — asserting the release REASON, not merely that the next start did not fail.

A runtime arm cloned from repository-delivery-runtime.test.ts:67-80 minus the file write asserts the derived fact is the new pre-intent value (not "REFUSED") and that a post-intent refusal such as GIT_COMMIT_FAILED still derives "REFUSED" and still blocks — the two buckets are asserted separately so the fix cannot be a blanket un-block.
A lander arm asserts NOTHING_TO_COMMIT records its refusal receipt with NO journaled landing intent, pinning the property the release depends on.

A recovery-evidence arm proves an already-BLOCKED reservation whose durable receipt is NOTHING_TO_COMMIT and which has no journal intent is offered a release by repository.recover instead of REPOSITORY_RECOVERY_CONTAINMENT_UNKNOWN — and that a BLOCKED reservation WITH a journal intent still answers CONTAINMENT_UNKNOWN.

The two-process reproduction the review described (real temp git + real sqlite: verify passes, land NOTHING_TO_COMMIT, next independent node claims) is committed as an arm and its pre-fix RED is quoted in the completion record alongside the post-fix green.
docs runbook states what NOTHING_TO_COMMIT does to checkout ownership and how a wedged pre-fix checkout is released; `BLOCKED: []` in repository-execution-port.ts is unchanged.

pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test EXIT 0 with its count line quoted; the goal-landing-facts.ts:66-67 question (does a nothing-landed node count as landed for goal.close) is either answered in this row with an arm or filed as a named follow-up row in dependsOn of the unattended-journey row.

implementationPlan.description:
READ THE CHAIN. NO EDITS. Every anchor below was measured at HEAD and independently confirmed against the filing's own anchors, so this step is confirmation, not discovery.

1. node-lander.ts:207-211 — `delivered.length === 0` refuses `{ code: "NOTHING_TO_COMMIT", detail: "no path in the workspace differs from the staffing baseline" }`. It fires BEFORE `commitJournaledLanding` at :222-223, so NO landing intent is journaled. That is the property the whole fix rests on: the outcome is provably effect-free.
2. repository-delivery-runtime.ts, in `readRepositoryDeliveryFacts`: `return landed.receipt.outcome === "COMMITTED" && landed.receipt.commit !== null ? "LANDED" : "REFUSED";` — one ternary folds pre- and post-intent refusals into one bucket. The defect is here.
3. repository-delivery-coordinator.ts:164-167 — `if (facts === "LANDED") { release(handle, "LANDED"); return; } else if (result === "RETRY" && facts === "ACCEPTED") change(handle, { phase: "AWAITING_LANDING" }); else block(handle);`. The block is the ELSE.
4. repository-execution-port.ts:98-101 — the release table admits exactly four reason@phase pairs and refuses everything else REPOSITORY_EXECUTION_TRANSITION_INVALID.
5. repository-execution-port.ts:12 — `BLOCKED: []`, terminal.
6. repository-recovery-evidence.ts:38-40 — a BLOCKED reservation with no journal completion answers REPOSITORY_RECOVERY_CONTAINMENT_UNKNOWN, so ADMIN recovery cannot release it.

UNDERSTAND WHY THIS IS HIGH AND NOT COSMETIC, because it changes how carefully you treat the release: the block is durable in `<gitdir>/moe-repository-execution.sqlite` and SURVIVES DAEMON RESTART; repository-execution-port.ts:30 refuses ANY effect family while the record exists, so publish and criterion verification on that checkout are shut out too; and it is reachable by default — scripts/up.ps1:48 sets MOE_NODE_WORKSPACE and never MOE_NODE_LANDING, so agent-wrapper-main.ts:151-153 resolves landingOn=true for every node.deliver spawn.

CENSUS THE UNION BEFORE WIDENING IT: `git grep -n "RepositoryDeliveryFacts\|readRepositoryDeliveryFacts" -- 'apps/**' 'packages/**'`. Expect the declaration at repository-delivery-contracts.ts:14, the port interface at :18, the runtime, and three test files (coordinator.test.ts:25,39; recovery.test.ts:24,43; runtime.test.ts:78,93,101,119). Confirm NO exhaustive `switch` exists; if one has appeared since planning it is an owned path and you must say so before editing.

ALSO FOUND, not in the filing: the SAME wedge is reachable from the LANDING branch at :170-175 (`facts === "LANDED" ? release : block`) — that is the daemon-death-after-refusal path, and step 4 must release there too or the fix leaves a second door open.
4. repository-execution-port.ts:98-101 — four reason@phase pairs, else REPOSITORY_EXECUTION_TRANSITION_INVALID. :12 `BLOCKED: []` terminal. :30 acquire refuses while any record exists.
5. repository-recovery-evidence.ts:40-42 (filing said :38-40) — BLOCKED + (no journal or completion===null) -> REPOSITORY_RECOVERY_CONTAINMENT_UNKNOWN.

CENSUS OF THE UNION, `git grep -n "RepositoryDeliveryFacts\|readRepositoryDeliveryFacts" -- apps/** packages/**`: 16 hits, exactly the set the step predicted — contracts.ts:14 (type) and :18 (port interface), runtime.ts:22,37,39,72, coordinator.test.ts:10,25,39, repository-delivery-recovery.test.ts:12,24,43, runtime.test.ts:18,78,93,101,119. No new owned path has appeared since planning.

ONE MEASURED OBSTACLE TO STEP 3 AS WRITTEN, which changes the signature and is worth flagging before I get there. Step 3 says derive the new fact by reading the journal, "never by re-deriving what an intent is". The journal read is `readRepositoryLandingEvidence(store, handle)` and its key is `intentId(ownerDigest, baselineId, sessionId)` where ownerDigest = digest(projectId, nodeRef, storeId, ownershipToken) (repository-landing-intent.ts:22-24). `readRepositoryDeliveryFacts(store, projectId, nodeRef)` has NO handle, so it cannot compute that key today. The handle-free alternatives both fail: `store.getCommandDecision` needs the exact commandId, and enumerating `repository-landing:` aggregates would be an unbounded scan on the advance hot path (the exact shape that pegged the daemon loop in the affordances-read incident). So step 3 needs `facts: (nodeRef, handle?)` threaded from the coordinator, which has a live handle at all four call sites (:50, :141, :150, :164) and from runtime.ts:72. Test doubles that declare `(nodeRef) => ...` stay assignable, so the three test files above do not break. Absent handle will fail CLOSED to "REFUSED" (today's behaviour, blocks). I will do that in step 3 and record it there.

Write the two-process reproduction as a COMMITTED arm in apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/repository-delivery-runtime.test.ts — that file already builds a real temp git checkout and a real sqlite store, so use its `fixture()` rather than inventing a second harness. implementationPlan.description:
SEPARATE THE TWO REFUSAL BUCKETS AT THE FACT (repository-delivery-contracts.ts, repository-delivery-runtime.ts).

Add ONE member to `RepositoryDeliveryFacts` at repository-delivery-contracts.ts:14 meaning "the landing refused BEFORE any intent was journaled, so HEAD was never touched and nothing is owed on this checkout". The filing suggests REFUSED_NO_EFFECT; any name carrying that meaning is fine, but name it for the PROPERTY, not for NOTHING_TO_COMMIT.

Derive it in `readRepositoryDeliveryFacts` by splitting the existing ternary: a refusal receipt with NO journaled landing intent yields the new value; a refusal WITH an intent still yields "REFUSED". Read the intent through the existing durable surface (node-lander-journal.ts / repository-landing-intent.ts, kind `internal.repository.landing_intent`), never by re-deriving what an intent is.

USE THE JOURNAL, NOT A CODE LIST. The filing floats a pre-intent set of "{NOTHING_TO_COMMIT, and arguably LANDING_BASELINE_MISSING / NOT_A_REPOSITORY}". The journal check resolves that "arguably" for free — any refusal decided before `commitJournaledLanding` has no intent and is effect-free by construction, and a future pre-intent code joins the bucket with no edit. A hand-kept code list needs maintaining and is wrong the first time someone adds a fourth code. If you find a refusal that journals an intent and still reports NOTHING_TO_COMMIT, stop: that would break the property step 5(c) pins.

DO NOT CHANGE WHAT "REFUSED", "LANDED", "ACCEPTED" OR "UNKNOWN" MEAN. This step narrows one bucket out of REFUSED and re-classifies nothing else.
implementationPlan.note:
THE TWO REFUSAL BUCKETS ARE SPLIT AT THE FACT, AND THE DISCRIMINATOR IS THE JOURNAL AS THE STEP REQUIRED — but it needed a signature change to reach the journal at all, which is the one thing I did beyond the step's letter. Recorded here because it changes an interface the step did not name.

WHAT LANDED
1. repository-delivery-contracts.ts: `RepositoryDeliveryFacts` gains `REFUSED_NO_EFFECT`, documented for the PROPERTY ("refused BEFORE any landing intent was journaled: HEAD was never touched and nothing is owed"), not for NOTHING_TO_COMMIT. REFUSED, LANDED, ACCEPTED, READY, SUBMITTED and UNKNOWN keep their meanings; nothing else is re-classified.
2. repository-delivery-runtime.ts: the ternary at the old :47 now reads `... ? "LANDED" : refusedFact(store, handle)`. `refusedFact` calls `readRepositoryLandingEvidence(store, handle)` — the existing durable surface for kind `internal.repository.landing_intent` — and answers REFUSED_NO_EFFECT only when it returns REPOSITORY_RECOVERY_EVIDENCE_MISSING, i.e. no intent row exists. Intent present, or ANY other read outcome, stays REFUSED. No code list anywhere: a future pre-intent refusal code joins the bucket with no edit, and a post-intent one cannot.

THE SIGNATURE CHANGE, and why the step could not be done without it (flagged in my step-1 note): the intent is keyed by `intentId(ownerDigest, baselineId, sessionId)` with ownerDigest = digest(projectId, nodeRef, storeId, ownershipToken) (repository-landing-intent.ts:22-24). `readRepositoryDeliveryFacts(store, projectId, nodeRef)` cannot compute that key. So it now takes an OPTIONAL 4th parameter `handle?: RepositoryExecutionHandle`, and `RepositoryDeliveryConfig.facts` is `(nodeRef, handle?) => ...`. The runtime passes it at the single production call site. The two handle-free alternatives were rejected on measurement: `store.getCommandDecision` needs the exact commandId, and enumerating the `repository-landing:` aggregate prefix would put an unbounded scan on the advance hot path — the shape that pegged the daemon loop in the affordances-read incident.

FAIL CLOSED WHEN THE HANDLE IS ABSENT: `refusedFact` returns plain REFUSED, which is today's behaviour and blocks. The dangerous direction is the other one, so absence can never widen the release.

BLAST RADIUS, measured not assumed: `git grep "RepositoryDeliveryFacts\|readRepositoryDeliveryFacts"` names one production consumer (runtime.ts:86) and three test files whose doubles declare `facts: (nodeRef) => ...`. A function of fewer parameters is assignable to a wider signature in TypeScript, so those doubles keep compiling unchanged; typecheck runs in step 6 and will say so rather than my asserting it here. No exhaustive `switch` over the union exists, so widening it breaks no exhaustiveness arm.

NOT YET WIRED: nothing consumes REFUSED_NO_EFFECT after this step — the coordinator still treats it as "not LANDED" and blocks, so behaviour at HEAD is unchanged and the step-2 red is still red. Step 4 is what makes it release.

implementationPlan.description:
RELEASE INSTEAD OF BLOCKING, THROUGH THE FENCE RATHER THAN AROUND IT (repository-execution-port.ts, repository-delivery-coordinator.ts, repository-recovery-evidence.ts).

(1) THE PORT'S RELEASE TABLE, repository-execution-port.ts:98-101. It is a ternary chain admitting exactly four reason@phase pairs — LANDED@LANDING, PUBLISHED@PUBLISHING, CRITERIA_COMPLETED@CRITERION_VERIFYING, and ABORTED_BEFORE_EXECUTION@RESERVED with `!prior.everExecuted` — and everything else is REPOSITORY_EXECUTION_TRANSITION_INVALID. Add ONE arm: a new release reason (the filing suggests LANDED_NOTHING) permitted from phase LANDING only. Do not relax the existing four and do not make the new reason phase-agnostic; this table is a fence, not plumbing.

(2) THE COORDINATOR, repository-delivery-coordinator.ts:164-167. Today: `if (facts === "LANDED") { release(handle, "LANDED"); return; } else if (result === "RETRY" && facts === "ACCEPTED") change(handle, { phase: "AWAITING_LANDING" }); else block(handle);`. Add a branch that releases on the new fact with the new reason, exactly as the LANDED branch does.
DO NOT REMOVE THE `else block(handle)`. A post-intent refusal such as GIT_COMMIT_FAILED must still block, because HEAD may already carry a partial landing. That deletion is the blanket un-block DoD 2 exists to catch and it would make every arm in this row pass.

(3) RECOVERY FOR CHECKOUTS ALREADY WEDGED BEFORE THIS FIX, repository-recovery-evidence.ts:38-40. Today any BLOCKED reservation with no journal completion answers CONTAINMENT_UNKNOWN, which is precisely this wedge. Admit a release when the durable landing receipt is a pre-intent refusal AND no journal intent exists. BOTH conditions, not either: a BLOCKED reservation WITH an intent and no completion is a genuine mid-write unknown and must keep answering CONTAINMENT_UNKNOWN.

(4) `BLOCKED: []` AT repository-execution-port.ts:12 STAYS EXACTLY AS IT IS (DoD 6). The release comes from not entering BLOCKED and from the recovery path above. Giving BLOCKED an outbound transition would remove containment for every other blocked cause on the board.
implementationPlan.note:
THE RELEASE GOES THROUGH THE FENCE. The step-2 red is now green: the 7 directly affected test files run `Test Files 7 passed (7) | Tests 49 passed (49)`, and `npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` in apps/daemon exits 0.

(1) PORT, repository-execution-port.ts:98. One arm added, not a relaxation: `reason === "LANDED" || reason === "LANDED_NOTHING" ? prior.state.phase === "LANDING"`. LANDING only, never phase-agnostic; PUBLISHED, CRITERIA_COMPLETED and ABORTED_BEFORE_EXECUTION (still `&& !prior.everExecuted`) are untouched, and everything else is still REPOSITORY_EXECUTION_TRANSITION_INVALID. The reason itself is declared in repository-execution-contracts.ts:5, which the step did not name but is where the type lives.

(4) `BLOCKED: []` at repository-execution-port.ts:12 IS BYTE-IDENTICAL. `git diff -- apps/daemon/src/repository/repository-execution-port.ts` touches exactly one line, the release ternary. Nothing gained an outbound transition from BLOCKED.

(2) COORDINATOR. `release()` widens to accept LANDED_NOTHING, and THREE branches now release on the new fact instead of blocking:
- AWAITING_LANDING (:168) — the branch the step named. `else block(handle)` is INTACT and still catches every other refusal.
- LANDING (:180) — NOT in the step, found in step 1. This is the daemon-death window: controller dies after the refusal receipt and before the release, and on the next advance the old code blocked. Releasing here too is what stops the fix from leaving a second door open.
- `owned()` (:50-56) — the adopt-an-orphan path, same window seen by a DIFFERENT controller. Was `phase === "LANDING" && facts === "LANDED"`, now also releases REFUSED_NO_EFFECT.
Every `config.facts(...)` call in the coordinator now passes its live handle (5 sites), which is what makes the journal discriminator readable. At EXECUTING (:146) REFUSED_NO_EFFECT is added to the BLOCK list on purpose: a landing outcome is unreachable from EXECUTING, and containment there must not change.

(3) RECOVERY FOR ALREADY-WEDGED CHECKOUTS. New `readRecoveryNoEffectEvidence` in repository-recovery-evidence.ts requires BOTH conditions and neither alone: `readRepositoryLandingEvidence` must answer REPOSITORY_RECOVERY_EVIDENCE_MISSING (no intent — if it answers ok, i.e. an intent EXISTS, the function returns CONTAINMENT_UNKNOWN itself), AND a durable landing receipt for the accepted verifier receipt must exist with `outcome === "REFUSED"`, `commit === null`, `refusal !== null`, matching subjectRef, verifierReceiptId and workspace. `readRecoveryLandingEvidence` is UNCHANGED — a BLOCKED reservation with an intent and no completion still answers CONTAINMENT_UNKNOWN through it.

TWO FILES BEYOND THE STEP'S LIST, and why the step could not close without them. The step said to admit the release in repository-recovery-evidence.ts alone. Measured, that alone ships a lie: the service's offer comes from `landing.ok`, and the release path then calls `git.guard(evidence)`, which dereferences `evidence.commit` and `evidence.binding` — a no-effect wedge has neither, so an "available" offer would fail inside the Git guard. Making the offer REAL needs (a) repository-execution-recovery.ts to admit a third proof kind LANDING_REFUSED_NO_EFFECT, permitted from LANDING or BLOCKED with a baseline and a session, leaving canAbort and canLand exactly as they were; and (b) repository-recovery-service.ts to fall back to the no-effect evidence for the offer and to release through it WITHOUT the Git guard, re-joining the durable evidence first and refusing EVIDENCE_CONFLICT if it moved. No new recovery ACTION was minted: RECONCILE_LANDED carries it, so REPOSITORY_RECOVERY_ACTIONS, the payload codec and the two control-room consumers of that roster are untouched.

NOT A BLANKET UN-BLOCK, which is the failure mode this row invites: the only path to a release is a receipt whose refusal is durable AND a journal with no intent. GIT_COMMIT_FAILED journals an intent before Git runs (node-lander-journal.ts:36-39), so it derives REFUSED and still blocks. Step 5(b) asserts both directions separately.

implementationPlan.description:
THE ARMS, EACH ASSERTING A REASON RATHER THAN AN OUTCOME (DoD 1, 2, 3, 4, 7).

(a) COORDINATOR, repository-delivery-coordinator.test.ts — with the REAL port: an ACCEPTED node whose landing refuses NOTHING_TO_COMMIT releases the checkout, `inspect()` answers a NULL reservation, and `start(node-b)` on the same root succeeds. DoD 1 is explicit that you assert the release REASON, not merely that the next start did not fail: a start succeeding for an unrelated reason proves nothing. Pre-fix this arm fails at the second claim with REPOSITORY_EXECUTION_BUSY.

(b) RUNTIME, repository-delivery-runtime.test.ts — clone the arm at :67-80 MINUS the file write so nothing differs from the baseline, and assert the derived fact is the NEW pre-intent value and NOT "REFUSED". Then a SECOND arm: a post-intent refusal such as GIT_COMMIT_FAILED still derives "REFUSED" and still blocks. DoD 2 requires these asserted separately; together they are what prove the fix is not a blanket un-block.

(c) LANDER, node-lander.test.ts — NOTHING_TO_COMMIT records its refusal receipt with NO journaled landing intent. This pins the property the release depends on: if a future edit ever journals an intent before that refusal, the release becomes unsafe and this arm is what says so first.

(d) RECOVERY, repository-recovery-evidence.test.ts, BOTH DIRECTIONS or it is vacuous — an already-BLOCKED reservation whose durable receipt is a pre-intent refusal with no journal intent is offered a release instead of REPOSITORY_RECOVERY_CONTAINMENT_UNKNOWN; a BLOCKED reservation WITH a journal intent still answers CONTAINMENT_UNKNOWN.

(e) DoD 7's ROUTED QUESTION IS ALREADY DECIDED AND FILED — do not re-open it. It is a second seam and it is now task-f7d38f752b074dc89da30631783aae04 ("a node that legitimately lands nothing never counts toward its goal"), filed with dependsOn on this row. Your job here is ONE arm in goal-landing-facts.test.ts pinning TODAY's behaviour: `landedGoals` skips any receipt whose `outcome !== "COMMITTED"`, so a node that refused NOTHING_TO_COMMIT does NOT join the goal's landed set. Do not change that behaviour in this row — the arm exists so the child row starts from a documented baseline instead of a guess.

Every arm names its expected code and, where two layers could answer, which one did (project rail 1).

comments.content:
ADVERSARIAL PASS (step-6). The five questions the step names, in order, answered from the code rather than from intent. Two of them changed the code; both changes are in this row.

1. "IF A NODE REFUSES WHILE A SECOND NODE HOLDS THE SAME ROOT, DOES THE RELEASE FREE SOMEONE ELSE'S CLAIM?" No, and it is now pinned. Only one reservation record exists per git directory, so a second node can hold the root only after the first was released. The port's release is a compare-and-swap on THREE things: `sameExecutionOwner` (which includes the ownershipToken), the exact revision, and the controllerId. A stale handle from the released node therefore cannot touch the next node's claim. New assertion inside the DoD 1 arm: after node-b claims, replaying node-a's own release answers REPOSITORY_EXECUTION_OWNER_MISMATCH and node-b's reservation is still there.

2. "CAN A REFUSAL REACH THE NEW FACT FOR A REASON OTHER THAN NOTHING_TO_COMMIT, AND IS RELEASING CORRECT FOR IT?" Yes, and yes. The reasons, enumerated from node-lander.ts by reading which refusals are decided before `commitJournaledLanding` at :227:
- LANDING_BASELINE_MISSING (:186) — the node was never staffed by the wrapper, so no baseline exists to diff against.
- NOT_A_REPOSITORY (:194) — `git.observe` found no repository.
- LANDING_VERIFIER_BINDING_MISSING, LANDING_VERIFIED_WORKSPACE_UNCONFIGURED, LANDING_VERIFIED_WORKSPACE_CHANGED (node-lander-verification.ts:28,29,33, reached at :222).
Releasing is correct for every one of them for the same reason: each is decided before any intent is journaled, so HEAD was never touched and the checkout is owed nothing. The node stays unlanded and its work stays in the working tree either way; the only difference is that the root is no longer owned. That is the point of naming the fact for the PROPERTY rather than for NOTHING_TO_COMMIT.

3. "IF THE DAEMON DIES BETWEEN THE REFUSAL RECEIPT AND THE RELEASE, IS THE CHECKOUT WEDGED IN A NEW WAY?" It was, in the first draft. The plan named only the AWAITING_LANDING branch; a controller that died right after the refusal leaves the reservation in LANDING, and the LANDING branch at coordinator :170 blocked on anything but LANDED. Both doors are now closed and both have arms: the same-controller restart (advanceOne's LANDING branch) and the different-controller adoption (`owned()`, after the old controller's pid is proven dead). Both release LANDED_NOTHING on the same durable evidence, and `land` is NOT called again — the landing is never repeated.

4. "CAN RECOVERY RELEASE A CHECKOUT WHOSE HEAD DID MOVE, IF THE JOURNAL WRITE ITSELF FAILED?" No, in both directions of the write order (node-lander-journal.ts:36-51). If the INTENT write fails, git never runs, and the lander returns a REPOSITORY_RECOVERY_* code WITHOUT recording any receipt (node-lander.ts:229) — so the no-effect reader answers EVIDENCE_MISSING and offers nothing. If git commits and the COMPLETION write then fails, the intent EXISTS, so the reader answers CONTAINMENT_UNKNOWN. The dangerous case is the one that stays contained; the released case is the one where the intent was never written and git therefore never ran.

5. "CAN AN UNATTENDED RUN STILL BE STOPPED FOREVER BY ONE NODE THAT LEGITIMATELY HAD NOTHING TO COMMIT?" Not by the CHECKOUT, which is what this row owns: the reservation is released and the next node claims the same root, proven end to end against a real git checkout by the DoD 5 arm. The GOAL is a different matter and I am not claiming otherwise: `goalHasLandedCommit` still requires a COMMITTED receipt, so a goal whose only node legitimately landed nothing still has no landed commit and its publish offer stays withheld. That is the second seam, task-f7d38f752b074dc89da30631783aae04, and this row deliberately did not change it.

TWO HARDENINGS THE PASS PRODUCED, beyond the release branches:
- repository-execution-recovery.ts: the no-effect release now also requires `record.everExecuted`, matching the landing release. Unreachable today (a LANDING phase implies it), but the flag is the fence's own statement rather than an inference from the phase table.
- repository-recovery-evidence.ts: the no-effect reader now checks `baselineId` and `sessionId` are present BEFORE reading the journal. Without that, a reservation missing either would make `readRepositoryLandingEvidence` answer EVIDENCE_MISSING because the intent key cannot be COMPUTED, and the reader would have read an unanswerable question as "no intent was ever journaled". Same code, opposite meaning.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
THE FILING'S THREE-PART FIX SHAPE IS ADOPTED, and my own independent measurement reached the same chain before I had the description (the row arrived malformed; see codebaseInsights). The discriminator is THE ABSENCE OF A JOURNALED LANDING INTENT, not a code match.

WHY THE JOURNAL AND NOT A CODE LIST. The filing suggests the pre-intent set is "{NOTHING_TO_COMMIT, and arguably LANDING_BASELINE_MISSING / NOT_A_REPOSITORY}". Reading the journal instead of enumerating codes resolves that "arguably" for free: any refusal decided before `commitJournaledLanding` has no intent and is therefore effect-free by construction, and any future pre-intent code joins the bucket without an edit. A code list would need maintaining and would be wrong the first time someone adds a fourth code.

REJECTED — return "ACCEPTED" for a no-effect landing. It would release the checkout and then re-offer the node for landing forever: ACCEPTED is the fact that means a landing is still owed.

REJECTED — remove "REFUSED" from the coordinator's block path. That is the blanket un-block DoD 2 exists to catch: GIT_COMMIT_FAILED is decided AFTER an intent is journaled, so HEAD may carry a partial landing and must stay contained.

REJECTED — give BLOCKED an outbound transition. DoD 6 forbids it and it is right: `BLOCKED: []` is what stops a wedged reservation being walked out of containment by an ordinary phase change. The release comes from not entering BLOCKED, plus a recovery path for checkouts already wedged.

planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
THIS ROW IS A CLEAN REFILING. A malformed copy (task-5ee79dca) carried its description inside the TITLE argument, truncated at the 500-char cap with an empty description; it was deleted and refiled as this row minutes later. I had already measured the whole chain independently from the DoD alone before the description was recovered, and the two agree line for line — which is worth knowing, because it means the anchors below have been confirmed twice by different routes.

THE CHAIN, AND EVERY ANCHOR RE-MEASURED AT HEAD.
1. node-lander.ts:207-211 — `delivered.length === 0` refuses `{ code: "NOTHING_TO_COMMIT", detail: "no path in the workspace differs from the staffing baseline" }` and records a receipt with commit null. It fires BEFORE `commitJournaledLanding` at :222-223, so NO landing intent is ever journaled. Provably effect-free.
2. repository-delivery-runtime.ts, in `readRepositoryDeliveryFacts`: `return landed.receipt.outcome === "COMMITTED" && landed.receipt.commit !== null ? "LANDED" : "REFUSED";` — one ternary folds every refusal, pre- and post-intent, into the same bucket. This is the defect.
3. repository-delivery-coordinator.ts:164-167, measured verbatim: `if (facts === "LANDED") { release(handle, "LANDED"); return; } else if (result === "RETRY" && facts === "ACCEPTED") change(handle, { phase: "AWAITING_LANDING" }); else block(handle);`. So the block is the ELSE.
4. repository-execution-port.ts:98-101 — the release table is a ternary chain admitting exactly four reason@phase pairs: LANDED@LANDING, PUBLISHED@PUBLISHING, CRITERIA_COMPLETED@CRITERION_VERIFYING, ABORTED_BEFORE_EXECUTION@RESERVED with `!prior.everExecuted`. Anything else returns REPOSITORY_EXECUTION_TRANSITION_INVALID. A new reason permitted from LANDING is ONE added arm here.
5. repository-execution-port.ts:12 — `BLOCKED: []`, terminal by construction.
6. repository-recovery-evidence.ts:38-40 — `if (reservation.phase === "BLOCKED" && (!journal.ok || journal.completion === null)) return recoveryRefusal("REPOSITORY_RECOVERY_CONTAINMENT_UNKNOWN");`. The wedge has no journal at all, so ADMIN recovery cannot release it either.

THREE FACTS FROM THE FILING THAT RAISE THE SEVERITY, and none is guessable from the code alone:
- The block is durable in `<gitdir>/moe-repository-execution.sqlite` and SURVIVES DAEMON RESTART.
- repository-execution-port.ts:30 — acquire refuses ANY effect family while the record exists, so publish and criterion verification on that checkout are shut out too, not just landing.
- Reachable BY DEFAULT: scripts/up.ps1:48 sets MOE_NODE_WORKSPACE and never MOE_NODE_LANDING, so agent-wrapper-main.ts:151-153 resolves landingOn=true and wires the delivery runtime in front of every node.deliver spawn.
- The trigger is ANY seat that leaves `git status` clean at landing — including one that committed its own work — not only a task that needed no changes. node-lander.ts:73-79 records it firing live on UnAI on 2026-09-05.

THE UNION IS SAFE TO WIDEN. `RepositoryDeliveryFacts` is declared at repository-delivery-contracts.ts:14. A full-tree grep for the type name and the deriver returns only the declaration, the port interface at :18, the runtime, and three test files using it as a typed variable or asserting values (coordinator.test.ts:25,39; recovery.test.ts:24,43; runtime.test.ts:78,93,101,119). No exhaustive `switch` exists, so no consumer breaks — but all three must be read before the edit.

FILE SIZES, all well under the cap: contracts small, runtime 131, coordinator 199, execution-port 108, recovery-evidence 75, node-lander 272.
planningNotes.risks:
1. THE BLANKET UN-BLOCK IS THE FAILURE MODE THIS ROW INVITES. Deleting the `else block(handle)` at coordinator :167, or routing plain "REFUSED" to release, makes every arm in this row pass and ships a checkout that releases after GIT_COMMIT_FAILED — after HEAD may already carry a partial landing. DoD 2 requires the two buckets asserted SEPARATELY for exactly this reason.

2. THE RELEASE TABLE IS A FENCE, NOT PLUMBING. repository-execution-port.ts:98-101 admits four reason@phase pairs and refuses everything else with REPOSITORY_EXECUTION_TRANSITION_INVALID. Add ONE arm for the new reason, permitted from LANDING only. Do not relax the existing four, and do not make the new one phase-agnostic.

3. `BLOCKED: []` AT :12 IS LOAD-BEARING AND DoD 6 PINS IT. Anyone who "fixes" the transition table removes containment for every other blocked cause on the board.

4. THE RECOVERY HALF NEEDS BOTH DIRECTIONS OR IT IS VACUOUS. DoD 4: a BLOCKED reservation with a pre-intent refusal and no intent is OFFERED a release; a BLOCKED reservation WITH an intent still answers CONTAINMENT_UNKNOWN. A one-sided arm turns the containment gate off for real mid-write unknowns.

5. CAPTURE THE PRE-FIX RED BEFORE THE PRODUCTION EDIT. DoD 5 wants it quoted beside the green, and once the fix lands it is unrecoverable without reverting. This is why the reproduction is step 2, before any production change.

6. THE REPRODUCTION USES REAL GIT AND REAL SQLITE. repository-delivery-runtime.test.ts already builds that fixture — follow it rather than inventing a second harness, and close every store handle in a `finally`. A leaked sqlite handle on Windows makes the temp directory undeletable and the next arm inherits it.

7. DO NOT TOUCH THE `UNKNOWN` BRANCHES anywhere in this change. UNKNOWN blocking is fail-closed by design and is not this row's subject.
